approved_delicate_scopes.detail: The half-open positive real reduction interval[sqrt7,epsilon*sqrt7) is valid. Its y-coordinate bound is less than3sqrt(7/2)<6; y2..5 yields precisely the two seeds. Uniqueness of seed/exponent and negative-y sign transport are complete, rather than closure alone.

Multiplication matrix and norm a^3−4b^3+16c^3+12abc are correct; both displayed units have norm1. The transport of(-1,-3,0) to(-13,-2,4) keeps norm107 but leaves c0, correctly separating unit transport from a binary/global completeness theorem.

Darboux factorizations give levels0,3 for the scaled operator and k^2 times these for L. Positivity, one-dimensional kernels, partner-spectrum exclusion below threshold4, and relatively compact decaying potential establish the stated discrete and essential spectrum. The k2 example correctly scales to12/16.
Intertwining proves the entire sequence; the nonzero3x3 Hankel determinant4 and Cayley-Hamilton recurrence prove exact minimal order3.

Distance-shell sizes, quotient characteristic polynomial and trace equations correctly imply the42-vertex spectrum conditional on an actual graph with the stated intersection array. Graph existence and M22 transport are not inferred.

Binary histogram identity is a finite enumeration theorem; the degree3 integer-height difference is an exact polynomial certificate. It is not promoted to an unproved infinite Euler-product singularity.

Centered K is exactly the inverse of L+lambda*I on mean-zero vectors. Q-Cauchy-Schwarz proves a^2/Kii, and the explicit minimizer/uniqueness are correct. The three lambda2 constants5,15/2,3 are quadratic-energy minima; linear-in-height weight and integer asymptotic claims are explicitly kept outside the theorem.

Noetherian stabilization is used as eventual chain stabilization, not mistaken for one equal consecutive ideal. This gives an existential cutoff for fixed finite polynomial parameterization. The separate finite-dimensional word-closure argument is effective.
The384-to8 primitive phase map has exactly48 fibres by surjective reduction of units, hence the trace scaling48 is correct.

The264-root filter uses every root, whereas24 roots lose primitivity at11, leaving240 relative field embeddings. The excluded residue r4mod11, Euler degrees and polylog filter normalizationN^(1−s) are consistent.
Coefficient ratio and ODE match2arcsin(a/2)^2. Endpoint central-binomial majorant proves convergence; sine phase fixes the exact pi^2 denominator and branch.

Logarithmic derivative has the correct Ramanujan coefficient sign. D(s)=zeta(s)[240*30^(−s)+product(p^(1−s)−1)] cancels at2. Its derivative gives exactly−pi^2*(16log2+12log3+10log5)/180, with the Gamma derivative killed by D2=0. Absolute moment bounds justify integration and differentiation. No E8 lattice identification is inferred from the scalar kernel.

Log Fourier expansion has zero constant for the stipulated2x−2cos factors; Parseval and Bernoulli finite sum have the correct factors of2 and pi, including the doubled endpoint singularity. Rational coefficient955/867 is verified.

Determinant twist zeta^5 multiplies determinants byzeta^25 and killszeta^9; central cube gainszeta^30 and killszeta^4. Braid relations yield the conditional triangle quotient. Scalar determinant map exponent5 is inverted by7mod17, proving the direct compact product. No density or missing unitarization is claimed.
Norm-Euclidean Z[sqrt−2], parity and norm-coprimality prove the global two-point Mordell solution list. Coefficient b(3a^2−2b^2)=1 has precisely the stated cases.
Fibre-coset proof, halving quartic and rational doubling(129/100,−383/1000) are correct. Remaining sign/denominator and torsion obligations are explicit.
The inversion splitting at L=z^(−1/4) is exact and the signed error lies between−sqrt(z)/2 and0. Parameter/modulus convention, log4 constant and finite enclosures follow.
